datasets: NIBRS Group A / Part 1 Crime Data (data/crime.csv, NOT bundled; user must download)
311 Customer Service Requests 2024 (data/311.csv, NOT bundled; user must download)
synthetic fallback: data/sample/crime_sample.csv + 311_sample.csv generated by cmd/gensample
concurrency_primitives: goroutines; generic Load[T] pipeline with single reader -> bounded batch channel (workers*2) -> NumCPU parser workers -> collector; sync.WaitGroup; sync/atomic counters; sync.Map interner; atomic layout cache; lock-free map-reduce join with per-worker private maps merged after wg.Wait (BuildContext); five questions run concurrently writing to distinct slice indexes (RunAll)
design_patterns: Pipeline (ingest.Load), Strategy (RowParser[T], Question, Renderer), Factory (NewQuestion, NewRenderer), Builder (report.Builder); generics; all realized in code
questions: Where is combined public-safety (Part 1 crime) and 311 service burden highest, and how concentrated is it? (Mayor's Office)
Does 311 demand track crime, and which high-crime neighborhoods file unusually few 311 requests per crime? (Office of Neighborhood Engagement)
How do crime and 311 intake vary by hour of day, and do the peaks line up for staffing? (BPD & DOT)
Do neighborhoods with more blight-related 311 requests experience more Part 1 crime? (Planning / HCD)
Do high-crime neighborhoods wait longer for 311 requests to be closed? (DPW / Office of Equity)
stakeholders: Department of Planning / Housing & Community Development
Department of Public Works / Office of Equity
overview: Well-structured Go module (cmd/engine, cmd/gensample, internal/{model,ingest,analysis,report}) with a generic channel pipeline for ingestion, a lock-free map-reduce neighborhood join, concurrent question execution, and a Builder/Strategy/Factory report layer rendering ASCII charts and Markdown. Memory design (string interning, bounded channels, explicit GC with MemStats reporting) is explicit and measured. Code is idiomatic, tested, and the README matches it closely; the glaring gap is that no data ships with it.
stakeholder_value: The five questions are well framed for named agencies with findings, charts, tables and recommendations; on real data (verified with grader-supplied files) Q2's under-reporting ranking and Q5's resolution-time equity check are actionable, and Q4 quantifies the blight-crime association. Q3 is two single-dataset histograms rather than a join, and because the submission ships only a synthetic generator, the default run yields random-number 'findings' of no municipal value.
issues: data/ is empty: no real Open Baltimore data bundled and no fetch script; README requires manual download
run.sh automatically falls back to the synthetic generator, so the documented default run analyzes random data
Q3 (hour-of-day peaks) compares two single-dataset histograms rather than joining them
All records are materialized before the join (382 MB RSS on real 433 MB input) despite the 'memory stays flat' framing
No tests for report renderers or the questions' numeric outputs
Normalization by lead grader: rubric -3 applied because the synthetic generator is the default run.sh path (same treatment as Jessica Madu); real_data 5 -> 2, total 85 -> 82.
rationale: Build, concurrency, memory, architecture and README are all at the top of the rubric: real worker pools in parse, join and analysis, race-clean, tested, with realized design patterns. real_data is scored 5 because the submission contains zero data files and only a synthetic generator (the rubric's sample-only tier); runs_results and stakeholder are trimmed because the out-of-the-box run is on synthetic data and Q3 is single-dataset. Total 85, B.
